div.head: CHn cor 1.2
div.ab: Et omnes malas consuetudines, quibus regnum Angliæ iniuste opprimebatur, inde aufero: quas malas consuetudines ex parte hic pono.
Et omnes malas consuetudines quibus regnum Angliae iniuste opprimebatur inde aufero, quas malas consuetudines ex parte hic pono.
And I abolish all the evil practices with which the realm of England was unjustly oppressed, and these evil practices I herewith set down in part.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 276–277 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text added from Gesetze I p. 521, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

note.seg: Aufrechte (‘Antiqua’-)Buchstabennoten beziehen sich auf Band II: Erklärungen.
Upright (‘Antiqua’, i.e. roman) letters used as note-markers refer to Band II: Erklärungen.

Das Folgende betrifft das regnum im Gegensatz zur ecclesia in 1, 1. Nur die Sätze 2—5. 7—8. 10 betreffen fiskale Missbräuche, nicht 5, 1—6, 1. 8, 1—9. 11—14, 1. Meist (2ff. 10) schiebt Heinrich jene dem Bruder zur Last, teilweise (5. 8) dem Vater.—Das letzte Wort{21} liest suppono auch Rs.—Diesen Satz benutzt Heinrichs II. Freibrief: omnes malas consuetudines, quas [Henricus I.] delevit

What follows concerns the regnum, as opposed to the ecclesia in 1, 1. Only clauses 2—5. 7—8. 10 concern fiscal abuses, not 5, 1—6, 1. 8, 1—9. 11—14, 1. Henry mostly (2ff. 10) lays the former to his brother’s charge, partly (5. 8) to his father’s.—The last word{21} is read suppono by Rs too.—This sentence is used by Henry II’s charter of liberties: omnes malas consuetudines, quas [Henricus I.] delevit
